A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SARM and RA-BC. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A.1–A.8 support reliable comparison, including matching material relocated between versions.

before.justification: v3 reports original reward-model evaluations, real-robot T-shirt folding experiments, ablations, dish-unloading evaluations, and simulated reinforcement-learning results in Appendix A.8.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and adds REDS and VICtoR comparisons and a brightness-perturbation evaluation in Table 1.

M1.justification: The stage/subtask architecture, progress-label construction, training objectives, rewind augmentation, and RA-BC weighting procedure remain unchanged. Appendix A.8 also retains the same RA-QL adaptation.

E1.justification: v4 adds brightness-perturbed T-shirt observations as an input-condition test scenario. T-shirt folding, dish unloading, and simulated cube picking were already evaluated in v3; moving dish unloading into Section 4.1 does not add task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds evaluated REDS and VICtoR baselines alongside GVL, VLC, LIV, and ReWiND. This substantially broadens the central reward-model comparison, particularly through the directly relevant stage-aware REDS comparator. Dish-unloading and policy-learning comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The added SARM (VB) evaluation perturbs each frame's brightness by up to ±0.3. Existing data splits, evaluation metrics, rollout counts, and policy-training budgets remain unchanged. Newly stating that applicable baseline encoders match SARM's model size does not establish a revision to existing experiments.

E4.justification: Section 4.1 and Table 1 add a controlled brightness-robustness test. Existing annotation, rewind, model-scale, input-modality, temporal-sampling, reward-quality, and qualitative rollout analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Repeated-evaluation information is unchanged, including four policy trials per shirt color and ten simulation rollouts per checkpoint. v4 adds no seed reporting, confidence intervals, significance tests, or other uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds DemoL/rollout-rho results for REDS (0.036/0.16), VICtoR (0.079/0.00), and brightness-perturbed SARM (0.015/0.78), plus classification breakdowns. Retained numerical results and appendix curves are unchanged. The new REDS and VICtoR rho values conflict with their displayed classification totals, limiting interpretation of those scores.

T1.justification: Equations 1–11 retain the same definitions and mathematical procedures, including progress targets, RA-BC weighting, rollout classification, and discounted return. No theorem, proof, assumption, or substantive derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The core SARM and RA-BC contributions, robustness claims, and headline 83%/67% policy success claims are retained. The added conclusion sentence about reinforcement learning summarizes the already existing Appendix A.8 experiment rather than introducing a new contribution.

C2.justification: v4 adds interpretations of VICtoR's pessimistic predictions and REDS's difficulty producing dense progress estimates, and interprets SARM (VB) as evidence of lighting robustness. Existing explanations of annotation diversity, rewind augmentation, and policy improvement remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v4 newly states that applicable baseline transformer encoders are matched to SARM's model size and clarifies serious annotation errors with concrete examples. Existing architecture specifications, optimizer settings, hardware, policy hyperparameters, and project-access information are retained.

R1.justification: Sections 1–2 add VICtoR, REDS, DrS, and data-quality/data-curation work by Belkhale, Dass, and Agia. A focused new paragraph distinguishes SARM from stage-aware predecessors through visual inputs, continuous progress, and dedicated stage estimation; the broader research framing remains intact.

P1.justification: The abstract is condensed and rewritten, Section 4.1 is reorganized around both retained tasks, and the conclusion gains an existing RL finding. Local edits clarify BC baselines, correct architecture-figure references, and update contact information and publication headers. The overall section structure remains stable.

P2.justification: Table 1 expands by three columns and uses a denser display. The unchanged dish-unloading table moves from Appendix A.6, Table 9, to main-text Table 2. Appendix Figures 13–14 are redistributed across pages; existing figure content is retained.

improvement.justification: The added relevant baselines, brightness test, and clearer positioning against stage-aware predecessors modestly strengthen the paper. However, Table 1 reports REDS/VICtoR rho values of 0.16/0.00 although their classification counts imply 0.50/-0.17, weakening the added comparison. These inconsistencies temper the benefits without reversing the displayed advantage of SARM. The methods and headline policy outcomes remain unchanged.
